object_description: two-storey flat Z-shaped building with a ring-shaped break roof linking it to the old school
geometry_property: ring-shaped break roof with open middle
design_condition: the flat building is clearly subordinated to the historic school and its mirror-symmetrical figure adapts the large footprint to the surroundings, with a ring-shaped break roof joining old and new into one place of arrival

positive: The two-storey flat building is clearly subordinated to the historic schoolhouse
It leaves no question open about the hierarchy between old and new
The mirror-symmetrical basic figure adapts the relatively large footprint to the surroundings
Two small forecourts are articulated, with the biotope and garden well located
A ring-shaped break roof connects new and existing building with surprising naturalness and elegance
The inconspicuous roof with the open middle gives the two-part school a single common place of arrival
This clarity in address formation is a remarkable contribution to the complex as a whole
The subordinating attitude continues coherently in the architectural expression
The subtle differences between the two floors and the rhythm shifts are beautiful
They are well coordinated with the support system
The wood element facades follow a desire for contemporary sustainability and sober functionality
The result is a solid, calm and functional pavilion architecture of great relaxation
The central internal access offers good orientation
The classroom floor offers an attractive multi-use range of space with real quality of stay
The zones for learning, playing and informal communication are very well exposed
They leave an appealing atmosphere and are fully usable thanks to two external escape stairs
The immediately assigned terraces are an extremely promising addition to everyday school life
The two-storey building allows all classrooms on one floor, aiding exchange between all classes
The internal group rooms are naturally lit and generously glazed to the classrooms
Visibility is optimally guaranteed everywhere
The ground floor sensibly accommodates all uses shared by both school buildings
Auditorium, library and foyer are directly accessible from the common place of arrival
The workrooms gain privacy by being raised to the mezzanine
Concentrating all workrooms is welcomed operationally and as an appealing face to the outside
The teachers rooms offer a good retreat with a covered outdoor area
Locating the kitchen close to the entrance lets it serve the covered outdoor area directly
A tried and tested reinforced concrete skeleton with reasonable spans was chosen
Non-load-bearing lightweight interior walls separate primary and secondary structure clearly
This allows a free division of the internal organisation
The integration of higher rooms and a minimal basement promise good profitability
The comparatively small floor area and building volume contribute to this
The rational construction with repetitive elements reduces construction costs
The project gets to the heart of school operations with craftsmanship and healthy pragmatism
A rich offer of lounge, learning and play areas has been created with controlled means
Spatially differentiated transitions create a broad repertoire between retreat and encounter
The break roof is a real invention as an identity-creating and mediating element
negative: The direct assignment of the cloakrooms to the classrooms is not completely resolved
The location of the teachers rooms is not quite ideal due to their distance from the entrance
The densification idea of two extra classrooms would massively weaken the core project idea
The project is little compact due to the small number of floors and the individual jumps
